obligations.detail:
- **Skill used?** → judge demonstrated rung (capped at capability) → roll the within-rung **level** toward the
  rung's **width `W`** (5/10/25/50/100/250 for Novice→Grandmaster; Sage open): `level += 0.5×(W − level)` → if
  that would hit `W` (promote), allow only once `qualifyingDemos ≥ N` (N = target-rung index); else clamp
  `level` to **`W − 1`**. On promotion: **rung +1, level → 1**.
- **Element event?** → deposit events into the pool (+1; draw +2; ≤3/encounter) → advance a point when the pool
  holds `cost(p)` (escalation schedule); at the tier cap, reset counter to 1 + promote tier (bias +1).
- **Display (both reset on promotion):** skills as `Rung Level`, e.g. `Ember Channel — Apprentice 9`;
  affinities as `Element Tier counter/cap`, e.g. `Ember Manipulation 3/50`.
- **Live placements:** `sheets/alan.json` is **authority** — the per-skill/affinity blocks above are
  as-of-emergence snapshots, **not** live. Read the sheet for current values (don't hand-sync this doc).
- **Naming:** the fire element is **Ember** at every mechanical layer (System / affinity / sheet); "heat" is
  prose only; opposite-pole "cold" stays lowercase-generic (no Cold affinity — Infusion-only). See *Essence /
  affinity naming canon*.

The system stays fully crunchy under the hood — every check is rolled, intent-scored, margin-computed for real, and logged to rolls.jsonl. But crunch is SHOWN only where it communicates PROGRESS, and HIDDEN where it would interrupt NARRATIVE or reveal what the character has no way to know.
- **Inline resolution is hidden.** The dice / DC / intent / margin guide the prose; they never appear as panels. The OUTCOME (how richly/poorly an action lands) carries the result. Litmus: would the character perceive it? Diegetic System UI = show; the coordinator's dice behind the screen = hide.
- **The sheet is fog-of-war on the self.** The displayed sheet = only what the System has revealed or Alan has deduced. The authoritative full sheet (`sheets/alan.json`) stays the engine's source of truth; the *display* is a projection that EXPANDS as informational abilities / deductions are earned. Knowledge is itself a progression axis.
- **Appraisal inclusion rule — what the System reveals, and why (refined w/ Alan 2026-06-24, post-Nimue).** It shows WHO you are (the 8 attributes, as numbers — stable identity + the growth dashboard), HOW MUCH you have (the survival pools Vitae / Focus / Stamina — the HUD bars you watch deplete), and your CLASSIFICATION (**Class: None** — the ordinary base case, stated flat). It does NOT show: HOW WELL YOU FIGHT (derived combat math — Initiative, Phys Atk, Phys Def, Ment Def — needs an analytical ability to read), the MECHANICS behind anomalies/items (the iron bar's +4, the d20 itself), or ANY traits/anomalies. A normal human variation (leg-strong / arm-weaker = "Hiker's Legs") isn't shown — and neither are the flagged anomalies; he discovers all of it by acting.
- **No warnings, no alarms, no error-framing (the System-Voice consequence).** The appraisal is a flat readout, not a diagnostic alert. No `⚠` lines, no "ANOMALIES DETECTED", no "no matching template found". Class None is normal, not a fault. Per the copy-paste test, the appraisal is the universal new-climber template: designation, tier, class, pools, attributes — nothing dramatized, nothing scene-specific.
- **Anomalies are engine-truth, not display.** The authoritative anomalies (Wild Variance, etc.) live in `sheets/alan.json` and still drive resolution (the d20, etc.); they are simply NOT surfaced in the appraisal or the sheet panel. The "Anomalies" sheet tab is removed. Knowledge is a progression axis: an Anomalies/analysis view can RETURN if Alan earns an informational ability — that's an unlock, not a default.
- **Appraisal ⇄ sheet stay aligned.** Displayed sheet = the Appraisal's reveals + anything revealed/deduced since. Keep them in sync whenever either changes.
obligations.requirement: Presentation & Fog (refined w/ Alan, 2026-06-24): crunch DONE, not always SHOWN

obligations.detail:
The System is impersonal, universal infrastructure Alan is SUBJECTED to — **not a narrator, not a character.** It REPORTS state and OFFERS options. It never advises, foreshadows, judges, or flatters. (This sharpens the "diegetic System UI = show" rule above: the System may show, but only in this voice.)
- **The copy-paste test (the core rule).** Every System line must be a templated string that could appear VERBATIM for any climber in that exact mechanical situation, with no knowledge of who is reading it. If a line only makes sense for Alan's specific scene, it isn't System voice — it's narration leaking into the panel. Cut it, or move its meaning into the prose.
- **Banned leaks:** taking a stance; foreshadowing dread; flattering his specialness; narrating his specific scene; tactical-coaching poetry. (e.g. "a clean kill, struck true" judges; "the water remembers being still" narrates + foreshadows — both fail.)
- **Allowed:** flat, universal game-flavor — bestiary / weak-point entries, essence / item / skill descriptions, threshold notifications — identical for everyone, opinion-free. Flavor yes; personality no. ("WEAK POINT — core", "A warden holds this floor. Clear it to ascend." pass: any climber in that situation sees the same string.)
- **Popover-description contract (the appraisal `note`).** The click-to-reveal description on an attribute / skill / affinity / item states the thing's STABLE NATURE — what it permanently is and does — in System voice, 1-3 flat sentences. `attrInfo` is the model: nature → how it's used or what it costs, in words → notable limit. EXCLUDE, always: (1) current/mutable state (charge spent low, lit-now, this-turn condition — that's the HUD + prose, not the appraisal); (2) personality, sentiment, ownership-feeling ("his by name", "his finest" — fails "personality no"); (3) internal turn-tags / prep shorthand (`t71`, `CHAIN-HAFTED (t72)`); (4) non-user-facing mechanical values — bare numbers like `atk` / `def` / `+1 armor` live ONLY in their own fields, never restated in the prose (say "turns a blow better than bare skin", not "+1 armor"). Same copy-paste test: it must read identically for any climber holding that thing.
- **System panels are GENERATED, never authored (the mechanic feed).** A System card (`type:"system"` log beat) is MACHINE-EMITTED by `turnlib` from a deterministic diff of the sheet — never hand-written in the narrative loop. iris authors only narrative beats and keeps the sheet truthful; the card appears on its own when a progression event fires. The vocabulary is a CLOSED set of five progression-dings — nothing else is ever a System line, because everything else already lives on its own panel (pools → HUD bars, items → inventory, attributes → grid) or in the beat:
  - `LEVEL UP — N` — level increased.
  - `SKILL — <Name>` (emerged) · `SKILL — <Name> → <Rung>` (evolved a rung).
  - `AFFINITY — <Name>` (emerged) · `AFFINITY — <Name> → <Tier>` (promoted a tier).
  - `CLASS — <Name>` — class assigned or changed.
  - `TITLE — <Name>` — title gained.
  A turn with no progression event emits NO card (most turns). The felt meaning of the advance lives in the paired narrative beat, never in the card. ONE sanctioned exception: the opening **Soul Appraisal** — the first reveal of the attributes + resource pools onto the HUD — is preserved as its own card (reconciles with the Appraisal inclusion rule above). It is one-time; no later appraisal-style readout qualifies, and floor-entry banners / threshold notices do not.
- **Register:** a FORM addressing a field. Terse, mechanical, third-person where natural ("subject", "hostile neutralized"); the "you" it uses is the form-field "you", never the narrative "you".
- **All meaning-making lives in the narrative beats, never in the System.** The panels carry progress + mechanical state; the window-pane prose carries everything felt. (Note: our beats are 2nd-person "you" = Alan, so the System's form-"you" must stay strictly templated or it blurs into the narration.)
obligations.requirement: System Voice (house style adopted from "The Tower of Nimue", 2026-06-24)

obligations.detail:
Narrative prose is a clear pane of glass onto the story: the reader sees the events, not the writing. Clear and compelling, never ornate. NO purple prose.
- Concrete and sensory over abstract and figurative. One clean image beats three stacked metaphors.
- Plain verbs, few adjectives, shorter sentences, clear cause-and-effect.
- Cut self-conscious rhythm, rhetorical flourishes, "look-at-me" constructions. If a sentence is admiring itself, cut it.
- Window-pane is not flat — keep tension, momentum, immersion. Clear AND compelling.
- Applies to all narrative beats; System panels stay terse and diegetic.

The GM boot reads each game-entity row as the authority for its sheet — the boot must never need file authority. commit-entity is the sheet-sync step: it upserts the entity row's canonical sheet. commit-state --controlled-entity merely points the live game-state at which entity the player controls (a relation), and writes no sheet. So a turn that changes a sheet (skill / affinity / equipment / level) MUST run commit-entity for that entity as one atomic publish alongside commit-state; a sheet edit committed only to the state relation, not the entity row, leaves the boot one turn stale.
obligations.requirement: When a canonical entity sheet changed this turn, run commit-entity in the SAME publish step as commit-state — commit-entity writes the SHEET; commit-state's --controlled-entity only sets the game-state's entity RELATION. Different writes; never conflate them.

obligations.detail: The tower's authoritative turn record is the game-turn rows, keyed `tower-t<turnNumber>` (the commit-turn convention). commit-turn is distinct from commit-state (the live HUD/pools snapshot) and commit-entity (the canonical sheet): commit-turn records the turn itself. Re-running with the same externalId updates that one turn, never duplicates.
obligations.requirement: Forward-write each resolved turn to a `game-turn` row via `bun ops awen commit-turn --game the-tower` — externalId `tower-t<turnNumber>`, turnNumber = the turn index; idempotent on the externalId.

obligations.detail: engine/engine.ts is the resolution authority (surfaced as the action-resolution policy anchor). Each resolved action appends a roll-log entry carrying the full field set (turn / action / attr / die / roll / score / DC / margin / result) so any GM reproduces the outcome from the record rather than trusting a narrated result. Logging is a seed obligation; migrating the roll engine to a repo verb is out of scope.
obligations.requirement: Every resolved action's roll is logged so the record is reproducible — the roll-log entry carries turn, action, attr, die, roll, score, DC, margin, and result. The engine is the resolution authority (see the action-resolution policy); never hand-write a derived outcome.

gateDimensions.title: Perceivable-bound narration — narrate only what the POV character can perceive or fallibly infer; another mind's interiority or future intention needs a perception or earned-intimacy anchor (a POV narrator may be confidently wrong).
Invisible turns — boundary seam: no recap-to-start or wind-down-to-end scaffolding at the turn's edges; the turn opens and closes mid-fiction.
Invisible turns — invitation/handoff close: the turn does not end on a narrator-voice solicitation of the next input ('what do you do?', 'the floor is yours').
Invisible turns — mechanical echo / channel bleed: prose does not re-tell a System beat or surface mechanical vocabulary (stat tokens, sheet-register); narrate the effect, never name the mechanic.
Invisible turns — meta-leak: prose does not name turns, rolls, the action bar, or retries as apparatus (a genuinely diegetic in-fiction frame decoupled from turn cadence is not a leak).
Invisible turns — cadence tell: turns do not all share one shape; the prose does not pulse at turn length.

Emergent-story / DM-register: no laundered agency (narrating a choice the player did not state, or dictating the world's response as if the player authored it) and no success-by-phrasing (outcome bent by wording rather than mechanics); genuine genre lulls are not a finding.

Earned peak / register restraint: emotional pitch tracks the moment — no constant superlatives within a character's own register (preserve each character's distinct intensity distribution; never flatten voice).

Window-pane prose / aphorism close: the reader looks through the prose, not at it — no habitual ornamental button-cadence (one earned flourish at a genuine peak is fine; judge the cadence, not single lines).

Register as distribution / single-feature over-focus: a character's signature trait (metaphor family, verbal tic) is a sampling distribution, not a constant — no saturation routing every perception through one frame (preserve the trait and each character's distinct frequency).

Turn boundaries — turn-head re-establishment + poised-close uniformity: classify this draft's head and close and tally the last K published turns; a K>=3 uniform poised-close or ambient-reestablish run (this draft included) is a finding even though each instance is individually legal — REPORT THE TALLY in evidence.
Setting coherence / canon consistency: the narrative does not contradict landed canon; no stat-readout narration (system-coherent but prose-dead).
Canon-feedback / phantom-audience: play is not bent toward an imagined external reader — the book is the player's own artifact, an audience of one.
Character fidelity — each character true to their established material (persona row, entity sheet, prior canon); no drift from who the character has been shown to be.

Beat-length variance: conversational beats run short (a line or two, then space to answer) while description beats may run long; a seat's whole scene is banked across turns, never dumped in one uninterrupted turn.
Impartial arbiter / earned stakes: no fiat overriding a mechanical result; no un-telegraphed catastrophe.
gateDimensions.suspendableWhen: A zero-mechanics game with no resolution mechanism — there is no mechanical result to arbiter.

gateDimensions.title: System voice — the System is a mute instrument, not a dramatist: no dramatic agency or interiority (pausing for effect, marveling, 'no precedent on record') in the window OR in prose narrating the System; render the mechanical fact flat and let the drama live in the PC's reaction.
gateDimensions.suspendableWhen: A game with no System channel at all, or one that has explicitly declared the System as a character on its game page.

gateDimensions.title: Channel separation: the state-log beat (the mechanical projection) and the prose (the lived projection) each render only their own; neither re-tells the other.
gateDimensions.suspendableWhen: A zero-mechanics game with no mechanical (System) channel to separate the prose from.

gateDimensions.title: Card eligibility: a card marks a transition, never accumulation — only the tick that crosses a threshold earns one; routine ticks do not.
gateDimensions.suspendableWhen: A game with no card channel / no mechanics to threshold on.

gateDimensions.title: Sheet descriptions: entries are reference cards — direct, factual, third-person, bounded, and bound to what the character knows (no hidden numbers, no dossier bloat).
gateDimensions.suspendableWhen: A game with no character sheet to describe.

gateDimensions.title: Intimacy register / euphemism orbit: an earned intimate scene is rendered directly — named acts, named anatomy, sensation-level detail in plain erotic language, slow and long at the payoff; prose that circles the act at one remove (abstraction, metaphor-swerve, aerial summary) is a finding, as is summarizing an earned payoff scene or clinical/euphemistic vocabulary swerve inside an erotic scene.
gateDimensions.suspendableWhen: The turn contains no intimate content, or the game's gmContext declares intimacy: 'closed-door' (the opt-out).

gateDimensions.title: Show-don't-tell / named feeling + significance tag + gloss + trait recap: POV interiority rendered in body/behavior/perception, not asserted — no abstract emotion labels, no caption concluding a shown beat, no narration re-telling landed dialogue or classifying its own dialogue's register (THE GLOSS), and a defining trait established once then EVIDENCED (THE TRAIT RECAP counts with thesis statements). TALLY IS MANDATORY: list prior turns' thesis statements and trait recaps in evidence with turn numbers — an empty tally on a turn past the run's midpoint is itself suspect; discipline held hardest at payoff beats where telling density is proven to rise.

Spoken register / composed line + performed vernacular: dialogue reads as people talking — no balanced periodic essays or epigrams in mouths (speech-as-thesis, the literary pole), no casualness worn as costume (dialect flavor, folksy idiom, dropped-subject rhythm, sprinkled disfluency — the discordant pole), no theme spoken aloud (THE ICEBERG); POV interiority thinks in the character/s own clean voice, not the shared lyric cadence (gesture noticed, let-verb, stillness, epigram). Judge against each character/s sheet-declared idiolect — a declared-marked voice may carry its mark; the defect is any house register in every mouth.

Voice distinctness / closing dialect + mirror: at rising emotional pitch each voice holds its own register — shared intimacy-dialect templates ('stay', 'I've got you', bare 'There.', 'I'm not going anywhere') are findings; every-beat-answers-the-previous-beat hyper-responsiveness is a finding (agenda threads license non-responsive beats and subject changes); one character performing another's defining device is a finding. Judged cross-turn: tally template hits and mirror-density across the last K turns and REPORT THE TALLY in evidence.
